Postcondition: the function applies `pte_val(pte) &= ~(_PAGE_WRITE)` to its local copy and returns that pte_t, so the _PAGE_WRITE bit is cleared and every other bit is unchanged; the caller's pte is not modified.

name: raw_copy_from_user
prose: Precondition: to is a kernel buffer of at least n writable bytes; from is a user address that may fault; n may be 0. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if n == 0. Faulting loads are recovered through the exception table (.fixup jumps past the failing chunk). Three paths. (1) If CONFIG_ARC_USE_UNALIGNED_MEM_ACCESS is off and either pointer is not 4-byte aligned, it copies byte by byte with a hardware loop, decrementing n after each completed byte; on a faulting load the loop is left and the function returns n, the exact number of bytes not copied. (2) If n is a compile-time constant it copies in ladder blocks of 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; each block loads its words first and then stores them, and its counter res (initially n) is decremented only when the whole block has been stored. A fault inside a block abandons that block only (the loaded words are not stored, while `from` may already have advanced past them), and the later smaller blocks are still attempted, so after a fault the copy is not necessarily a clean prefix and the data of later blocks can come from shifted source addresses. (3) If n is not a constant a single asm sequence copies the 16-byte chunks, then the remaining 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; a fault jumps to the end and abandons everything after the failing chunk, so only whole completed chunks are copied. In paths (2) and (3) the function returns res: n minus the sizes of the completed blocks, which is 0 when every block completed.
note: checked uaccess.h:138-336. Reviewer round 2 is right (in the constant-n path later blocks still run after a fault, with from advanced past the loaded-but-unstored words); round 15 (return overcounts) is not right: loads precede stores inside each block, so res counts every unstored byte of the failing block; the real hazard is that later blocks can still run.

name: raw_copy_to_user
prose: Precondition: to is a user address that may fault, from a kernel buffer of at least n readable bytes, n may be 0. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if n == 0. The exception-table entries are on the stores to user memory (labels 1, 11, 12, 13, 14-18), so faulting stores are recovered by a .fixup that jumps past the failing chunk. (1) If CONFIG_ARC_USE_UNALIGNED_MEM_ACCESS is off and either pointer is not 4-byte aligned it copies byte by byte, decrementing n after each completed store; on a faulting store the loop is left and the function returns n, the exact number of bytes not written. (2) For a compile-time constant n it copies in blocks of 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes (loads of the block, then its stores), subtracting the block size from res (initially n) only after the whole block was stored; after a fault the failing block is abandoned but the following smaller blocks are still attempted, and `from` may have advanced past the loaded words while `to` advanced only past the stores that completed. (3) For a non-constant n one asm sequence copies the 16-byte chunks and then 8, 4, 2 and 1 bytes; a fault jumps to the end and abandons every later chunk. In (2) and (3) it returns res, which counts the bytes of the failing block as not copied even if some of that block's stores (up to three 4-byte words of a 16-byte chunk) had already succeeded, so it is an upper bound on the bytes not written; it is 0 when everything was stored.
note: checked uaccess.h:370-529. Reviewer rounds 2 and 15 ('exception table covers loads, not user stores') are WRONG for raw_copy_to_user: labels 1:, 11:-13:, 14:-18: sit on the st.ab stores (e.g. lines 407-415, 475-499), unlike raw_copy_from_user where they sit on loads. Reviewer round 1 (remaining count of the failed chunk, not exact) is right.

name: __clear_user
prose: Precondition: to is a user address, n a byte count; the caller keeps ownership of the memory and the user stores are protected by the exception table. Postcondition: res starts as n. If the address is odd it stores one zero byte (res -= 1); then if the (new) address has bit 1 set it stores a zero halfword (res -= 2); so at most two alignment stores, up to 3 bytes, are issued before the count is looked at. It then loads lp_count with res >> 2 (arithmetic) and stores that many zero words, subtracting 4 each; then it stores a zero halfword if bit 1 of res is set (res -= 2) and a zero byte if bit 0 of res is set (res -= 1). A faulting store jumps to the end, skipping every later store without decrementing res for it. It returns res as unsigned long: n minus the bytes stored when no padding-underflow occurs, so 0 if every store completed (exactly the n bytes at to are zeroed), or the number of bytes not stored when a store faults. There is no guard for n smaller than the alignment padding (n < 3 with a misaligned to): in that case the padding stores can write beyond n bytes, res becomes negative, and the negative value is passed through the arithmetic shift into lp_count for the word loop (the loop runs for the huge count the hardware takes from it, if lp_count is treated as unsigned, until a store faults); a fault in the padding stores instead returns n or n - 1 (n - 2 etc. depending on which stores completed).
note: checked uaccess.h:530-576. Reviewers: round 1 (writes up to 3 bytes when n smaller than padding) right; round 2 (fault during padding returns n, not negative) right and stated; round 15 (at most two alignment stores) right: stb then stw. The behaviour of lp_count with a negative value is an inference from asr.f/lpnz, not verified on hardware.

name: __arch_swab32
prose: Statement-expression macro (three alternative definitions chosen by CONFIG_ARC_HAS_SWAPE and ARC_BSWAP_TYPE in swab.h); it is not a function definition.
note: macro, not a function.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE0(arc_gettls)
prose: Generated syscall function __do_sys_arc_gettls (process.c:41-44). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns task_thread_info(current)->thr_ptr, an unsigned long, converted to the syscall's long return type; it reads one field of the current thread's info and changes nothing. The value is whatever arc_settls last stored there ((unsigned int) of the user pointer), or the initial value if never set. Where long is 32 bits (32-bit ARC) a stored value with the top bit set becomes a negative long. No locks or references are taken.
note: checked process.c:25-44 and thread_info.h:43 (thr_ptr is unsigned long). The old claim that the result is always 0..4294967295 and never negative was wrong on a 32-bit long; contract removed.

name: processCFI
prose: Precondition: start and end delimit a readable CFI byte range, state points to a valid unwind_state, ptrType is the pointer encoding, targetLoc is 0 or a location to stop at. Because the advance_loc2 and advance_loc4 handlers read their operand bytes after only a check against end + 2 or end + 4 that cannot fail here (ptr is at most end after the opcode byte), up to 2 or 4 bytes beyond end can be read for those opcodes. Postcondition: returns 0 or 1. (a) If start != state->cieStart it first sets state->loc = state->org and runs processCFI over the CIE (state->cieStart..cieEnd, targetLoc 0); if targetLoc == 0 and state->label == NULL it returns that result at once (0 or 1). (b) Otherwise it executes instructions while result is non-zero and ptr < end: set_loc sets result 0 when read_pointer gives 0; advance_loc1 gives result 0 if ptr >= end; advance_loc2/4 set state->loc through advance_loc (always 1); DW_CFA_remember_state returns 1 (clearing state->label) when ptr == state->label, returns 0 when stackDepth >= MAX_STACK_DEPTH, otherwise pushes ptr; DW_CFA_restore_state returns 0 if stackDepth is 0, else it saves loc and label, sets label from the saved stack, resets cfa to badCFA, zeroes regs and stackDepth, recursively processes [start, end) with targetLoc 0 (its result becomes result) and restores loc and label; GNU_window_save and unknown opcodes set result 0; other opcodes update the rules or the cfa. After each instruction ptr > end sets result 0, and if result is non-zero and targetLoc != 0 and targetLoc < state->loc it returns 1. (c) After the loop it returns result && ptr == end && (targetLoc == 0 || state->label == NULL). state->loc, regs, cfa, stack, stackDepth and label can be partly modified even when 0 is returned.
note: checked unwind.c:693-815. Reviewer round 15 (advance_loc4 reads up to 8 bytes past end) is WRONG: ptr <= end after the opcode, so the 4-byte read stays within end+4. Round 1 (the end+2/end+4 checks do not reject over-reads) is right. Round 2 (augmentation) concerned an older wording.

name: PINMUX_PIN
prose: Object-like/function-like macro used to build pin-mux constants in a device-tree header; it is not a function definition.
note: macro, not a function.

name: bL_switcher_thread
prose: Precondition: arg points to a struct bL_thread (the thread's own slot) whose lock, wait queue and started completion are initialised. Postcondition: it sets the current task to low FIFO priority with sched_set_fifo_low(current) and calls complete(&t->started). It then runs a do-while loop (the body runs at least once): if a signal is pending it flushes it; it waits interruptibly on t->wq until t->wanted_cluster != -1 or kthread_should_stop() (the wait can also end because of a signal, its return value is ignored); under t->lock it copies wanted_cluster, completer and completer_cookie and sets wanted_cluster to -1 and completer to NULL; and if the copied cluster is not -1 it calls bL_switch_to(cluster) and then, if the copied completer is non-NULL, completer(completer_cookie). The loop ends when kthread_should_stop() is true after an iteration, and the function returns 0 (its only return). Because the request is cleared under the lock before the switch and the callback run, a new request may be accepted while the previous switch is in progress, and a request with a NULL completer can be overwritten by a later one before the thread services it.
note: checked bL_switcher.c:270-304. Reviewer rounds 1 and 2 are right and covered; the added points are the do-while shape and the signal flush.

name: ATOMIC64_OPS(add, adds, adc)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic64_add(s64 i, atomic64_t *v), produced by ATOMIC64_OP(add, adds, adc) inside ATOMIC64_OPS (atomic.h:311-326, 376-381). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic64_t whose counter is 8-byte aligned (ldrexd/strexd). Postcondition: after prefetchw it repeats ldrexd, adds on the low word, adc on the high word, strexd until the exclusive store succeeds, so v->counter becomes its previous value plus i (64-bit two's complement) without losing a concurrent update; there is no barrier in the function. It returns nothing. The same ATOMIC64_OPS(add, ...) invocation also generates arch_atomic64_add_return and arch_atomic64_fetch_add, which return s64 and are separate functions.
note: checked atomic.h:311-326. Reviewer round 15's omission of the return variants concerns other generated functions, not this one.

name: arch_read_trylock
prose: Precondition: rw points to an initialised arch_rwlock_t whose lock word is 4-byte aligned. Postcondition: after prefetchw it repeats ldrex of the lock word, computes old + 1, and executes strex of that sum only if the sum is non-negative as a signed value (strexpl), until the exclusive store does not fail. Then, with contended holding old + 1 (mod 2^32): if contended < 0x80000000 it issues smp_mb() and returns 1 (the lock word was incremented, which happens for old values 0 up to 0x7ffffffe, and also for old = 0xffffffff, which wraps to 0); otherwise it returns 0 with no store and the lock word unchanged (this covers a write-held lock, 0x80000000, and also old = 0x7fffffff, whose increment would reach 0x80000000).
note: slice cut the head: real function is arch_read_trylock (spinlock.h:248-271). Reviewer round 15 is right: 0x7fffffff is left unchanged and returns 0. The old-value 0xffffffff case is from tracing adds/strexpl, not from a documented use.

name: uaccess_save_and_enable
prose: Precondition: none; takes no arguments. Postcondition: one of three alternative definitions, chosen at build time. With CONFIG_CPU_SW_DOMAIN_PAN (always inline) it reads the domain register, sets the user domain to DOMAIN_CLIENT with set_domain and returns the old domain value. With CONFIG_CPU_TTBR0_PAN (always inline) it reads TTBCR, writes it back with the A1, EPD0 and T0SZ bits cleared, executes isb() and returns the old TTBCR. Otherwise it returns 0 and changes nothing. The caller is expected to pass the returned value to uaccess_restore. No locks, references or memory are transferred.
note: checked uaccess.h:29-69. The prose already matched the three variants; only the 'any context' remark was dropped.

name: arch_timer_arch_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs once at init (__init). Postcondition: it reads arch_timer_get_rate(); if that is 0 it returns -ENXIO (-6) and registers nothing. Otherwise it calls arch_timer_delay_timer_register(), which sets arch_delay_timer.read_current_timer to arch_timer_read_counter_long, sets arch_delay_timer.freq to a second reading of arch_timer_get_rate(), and calls register_current_timer_delay(&arch_delay_timer); it then returns 0.
note: checked arch_timer.c:20-42. Contract removed: the function writes a static delay_timer and registers it. Note the rate is read twice (lines 21 and 24).

name: watchpoint_handler
prose: Precondition: called from hw_breakpoint_pending for a synchronous (or asynchronous) watchpoint exception with preemption disabled; local interrupts may be enabled (hw_breakpoint_pending enables them if they were enabled in the interrupted context); addr and fsr describe the access and regs the interrupted context. Postcondition: returns nothing. It takes rcu_read_lock once, scans the per-cpu wp_on_reg slots (0..core_num_wrps-1) and releases the lock at the end. For each non-NULL slot: on debug architectures before v7.1 (only slot 0 allowed, BUG_ON otherwise) trigger is set to the watchpoint's configured address; on later ones, if debug_exception_updates_fsr() the access type derived from fsr must match the watchpoint type or the slot is skipped; the watchpoint value and control registers give the distance to addr, which updates the closest match, and only an exact match (distance 0) records trigger = addr. For an exact match: if the fault came from a uaccess routine (kernel mode and user-privilege watchpoint) no perf event is emitted and single-step is enabled; otherwise perf_bp_event is called and single-step is enabled only if the overflow handler is the default one. After the scan, if no exact match was found but some slot had a non-zero distance (min_dist > 0 and != -1), the closest slot gets trigger = addr, perf_bp_event is called for it, and single-step is enabled if its overflow handler is the default one (this closest-match path does not apply the uaccess check).
note: checked hw_breakpoint.c:727-820 and hw_breakpoint_pending (938-975). Reviewer round 15 is right: hw_breakpoint_pending may call local_irq_enable before this handler, so 'interrupts disabled' was wrong. Round 2 (one RCU read-side section around the whole loop) is right.

name: apply_relocate
prose: Precondition: sechdrs, strtab, symindex, relindex and module describe a loaded module image whose REL relocation section, target section, symbol table and string table are consistent and whose target sections already sit at their load addresses. Postcondition: it processes the Elf32_Rel entries of the relocation section in order and patches the target words in place. It returns -ENOEXEC, after printing an error and leaving the earlier relocations applied and the later ones unapplied, for a bad symbol index, an r_offset outside the target section, an ARM branch to a symbol with an odd (Thumb) address, a branch or PREL31 or LDR_PC_G2 relocation that is out of range (after trying a PLT entry via get_module_plt when CONFIG_ARM_MODULE_PLTS is set, for the branch types), a Thumb branch to an ARM function symbol, a Thumb branch out of range, or an unknown relocation type. It returns 0 after all entries were applied; R_ARM_NONE is ignored. No memory is allocated for the caller (a PLT entry may be allocated in the module).
note: the listed name apply_relocate_add does not exist in arm/kernel/module.c; the slice is the tail of apply_relocate (module.c:76-470) and the arch uses REL relocations. Checked all return statements (86-91 start of the function, 98, 103, 118, 151-156, 168, 223, 253, 354, 399, 462).

name: perf_reg_validate
prose: Precondition: mask is any 64-bit value. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (-22) if mask is 0 or mask has any bit set at or above bit PERF_REG_ARM_MAX (16), i.e. (mask >> 16) != 0; otherwise returns 0. No state is changed.
note: checked perf_regs.c:19-25 (REG_RESERVED = ~((1ULL << PERF_REG_ARM_MAX) - 1), PERF_REG_ARM_MAX = 16 from uapi/asm/perf_regs.h). Contract corrected to cover both outcomes.

name: spectre_v2_update_state
prose: Precondition: none; state and method are unsigned values (state is one of the SPECTRE_* levels, method a SPECTRE_V2_METHOD_* bit). Postcondition: the static variable spectre_v2_state becomes state if state is greater than its current value (otherwise unchanged), and the static variable spectre_v2_methods is ORed with method. It returns nothing.
note: the listed name spectre_v2_state is a static variable, not a function; the prose described spectre_v2_update_state (spectre.c:25-30), which is in the slice, so it is fixed under that name.

name: unwind_exec_insn
prose: Precondition: ctrl points to an initialised unwind_ctrl_block whose instruction stream (ctrl->insn, byte, entries) is set up and whose stack is readable at the addresses the instruction pops. Postcondition: reads one instruction byte with unwind_get_byte (which returns 0 with a warning if no entries are left, and decrements ctrl->entries each time a 32-bit word is used up) and returns URC_OK (0) or -URC_FAILURE. 0x00-0x3f adds ((insn & 0x3f) << 2) + 4 to ctrl->vrs[SP]; 0x40-0x7f subtracts it; 0x80-0x8f reads a second byte, fails if the 12-bit mask is 0, otherwise pops registers r4-r15 selected by the mask (a pop of r13 loads vrs[SP] from the stack; if r13 is not in the mask vrs[SP] is set to the advanced stack pointer after all pops); 0x90-0x9f except 0x9d and 0x9f copies vrs[insn & 0xf] into vrs[SP]; 0xa0-0xaf pops r4 to r4+(insn & 7) and optionally r14, then sets vrs[SP] to the advanced stack pointer; 0xb0 sets vrs[PC] from vrs[LR] if vrs[PC] is 0 and sets ctrl->entries to 0; 0xb1 reads a mask byte, fails if it is 0 or has bits 4-7 set, otherwise pops r0-r3 per the mask and sets vrs[SP] to the advanced pointer; 0xb2 adds 0x204 + (uleb128 << 2) to vrs[SP]; any other opcode, including 0x9d and 0x9f, warns and fails. On a failure from a pop, vrs[SP] is unchanged but earlier popped registers in vrs[] may already be overwritten; on every path the instruction stream position and ctrl->entries reflect the bytes consumed. No locks are taken and no memory is allocated.
note: checked unwind.c:211-333 (get_byte, pop helpers) and 337-408. Reviewer round 15 is right (a popped r13 loads vrs[SP] rather than advancing it); round 2 right (r13 is the last register so a later pop cannot fail); round 1 partly right (vrs[SP] unchanged on failure, as I found). Old prose said ctrl->entries unchanged on failure; unwind_get_byte decrements it as bytes are consumed.

name: xscale_cp0_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs once as a late initcall. Postcondition: returns 0 on every path. If the CPU is not in the XScale family it returns 0 without touching anything. Otherwise it reads the coprocessor access register, clears bits 0-1 and writes the value with bit 0 set, then probes for iWMMXt. If iWMMXt is detected and CONFIG_IWMMXT is not set it only prints a warning (no notifier, no hwcap change). If detected and CONFIG_IWMMXT is set it prints an info message, sets HWCAP_IWMMXT in elf_hwcap, registers the iWMMXt thread notifier and the iWMMXt undefined-instruction handler. If iWMMXt is not detected it prints an info message, registers the DSP thread notifier and sets bit 0 in the access value. It finally writes the access value (bits 0-1 clear in the iWMMXt cases, bit 0 set in the DSP case) back to the coprocessor access register.
note: checked xscale-cp0.c:150-180. The old contract was dropped because the function changes coprocessor and global state; the prose already matched the code.

name: exynos_cpu_power_state
prose: Precondition: cpu is a core index for which EXYNOS_ARM_CORE_STATUS(cpu) designates a readable PMU register. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value read with pmu_raw_readl from that register ANDed with S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN (0x3, include/linux/soc/samsung/exynos-regs-pmu.h:183), converted to int, so the result is 0, 1, 2 or 3 and is non-zero when either of the two low bits is set. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: checked platsmp.c:129-133. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN is 0x3 in this tree, so the range 0..3 is right; the claim 'nonzero exactly when the power-enable bit is set' is refined to 'either low bit'.

name: exynos_cluster_power_state
prose: Precondition: cluster is a cluster index for which EXYNOS_COMMON_STATUS(cluster) designates a readable PMU register. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value read with pmu_raw_readl from that register ANDed with S5P_CORE_LOCAL_PWR_EN (0x3), converted to int, so the result is 0, 1, 2 or 3 and is non-zero when either of the two low bits is set. It takes no lock and allocates nothing.
note: checked platsmp.c:159-163. Reviewer round 15 is WRONG: the constant is 0x3 (exynos-regs-pmu.h:183).

name: tzic_set_irq_fiq
prose: Precondition: only built with CONFIG_FIQ (otherwise tzic_set_irq_fiq is #defined to NULL); tzic_base is mapped. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (-22) without touching a register when (hwirq >> 5) >= 4, i.e. hwirq >= 128. Otherwise it reads INTSEC0 of bank hwirq >> 5, sets bit (hwirq & 31), clears that bit again if type is non-zero, writes the value back to the same register and returns 0.
note: checked tzic.c:52-67. Contract removed because the function accesses device registers; the prose already matched.

name: tzic_enable_wake
prose: Precondition: tzic_base is mapped and the TZIC was initialised by tzic_init_dt. Postcondition: writes 1 to the DSMINT register and reads it back; if the read-back is 0 it returns -EAGAIN (-11) without touching the wakeup registers; otherwise it copies each of the four ENSET0 bank registers into the corresponding WAKEUP0 register and returns 0.
note: checked tzic.c:207-221. Contract removed because the function accesses device registers; the prose already matched.

name: calc_dsor_exp
prose: Precondition: rate and realrate are unsigned long clock rates in Hz. Postcondition: returns -EIO (-5) if realrate is 0. Otherwise it halves a copy of realrate (integer division) up to three times and returns the smallest d in 0..3 for which realrate / 2^d (successive halving) is at most rate; if even realrate / 8 is greater than rate it returns 4, which callers must treat as invalid. It reads no other state.
note: checked clock.c:138-162. The old contract was dropped (round 15 right: realrate is modified in the loop so a postcondition on it needs the original value).

name: omap_readb
prose: Precondition: pa is a physical address inside the OMAP1_IO window that omap1_map_io statically maps (OMAP1_IO_PHYS, size OMAP1_IO_SIZE), so that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS(pa), which is pa - OMAP1_IO_OFFSET (0x00f00000), is its mapped device virtual address. Postcondition: returns the 8-bit value from __raw_readb of that address (0 to 255); a raw device read with no barrier, no locks and no allocation.
note: checked io.c:70-88 and hardware.h:64-65. Reviewer round 15 is right that OMAP1_IO_ADDRESS is a fixed subtraction valid for the OMAP1_IO window, so the DSP and DSPREG regions are not claimed any more.

name: omap1_cfg_reg
prose: Precondition: cfg points to a valid struct pin_config; no field is validated. Postcondition: if cfg->mux_reg is non-zero it reads that register under mux_spin_lock (irq-saving), replaces the three bits at cfg->mask_offset with cfg->mask, writes it back and releases the lock; warn is set if the old three-bit field differed from the new value. If the CPU is not an OMAP15xx and cfg->pu_pd_reg and cfg->pull_val are both non-zero it does a locked read-modify-write of cfg->pu_pd_reg at bit cfg->pull_bit (set when cfg->pu_pd_val is non-zero, cleared otherwise), setting warn if the bit was not already in that state. If cfg->pull_reg is non-zero it does a locked read-modify-write of that register at cfg->pull_bit (cleared when cfg->pull_val is non-zero, set otherwise) and sets warn if the bit changes. warn is decided from the values read before each write, not from a read-back after it. With CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_WARNINGS it prints a warning when warn is set and returns -ETXTBSY if warn was set, otherwise 0; without that option it always returns 0. With CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_DEBUG it also prints the register values. No lock is held on return.
note: checked mux.c:286-409. Reviewer round 15 is right (warn compares the pre-write value to the desired one); round 2 right (pu_pd_reg touched only when pull_val is non-zero); round 1 right (return value depends on CONFIG_OMAP_MUX_WARNINGS).

name: omap3xxx_clockdomains_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at init (__init). Postcondition: returns nothing. If !cpu_is_omap34xx() it returns at once. Otherwise it registers the platform functions omap3_clkdm_operations and the common clockdomains, then reads omap_rev(): for AM35XX_REV_ES1_0 or ES1_1 it registers clockdomains_am35x and clkdm_am35x_autodeps; for any other revision it registers clockdomains_omap3430, then clockdomains_omap3430es1 when the revision is OMAP3430_REV_ES1_0 or clockdomains_omap3430es2plus otherwise, and clkdm_autodeps. It finishes with clkdm_complete_init().
note: slice cut the head: the function is omap3xxx_clockdomains_init (clockdomains3xxx_data.c:499-526), not clkdm_init. The old prose said exactly one clockdomain table; several tables are registered (common plus the revision-specific ones).

name: omap3xxx_cm_wait_module_ready
prose: Precondition: prcm_mod identifies a CM module; part is ignored; when idlest_id is in 1..3 the shift idlest_shift is below 32. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if idlest_id is 0 or greater than ARRAY_SIZE(omap3xxx_cm_idlest_offs) (3). Otherwise it polls the CM_IDLESTx register selected by idlest_id for the bit 1 << idlest_shift to read 0, at most MAX_MODULE_READY_TIME (2000) times with udelay(1) between polls, and returns 0 if the bit read 0 within that many polls and -EBUSY otherwise. It reads device registers and modifies no memory.
note: checked cm3xxx.c:88-107 and omap_test_timeout. The old contract was dropped because the function reads hardware registers.

name: omap2_control_base_init
prose: Precondition: none; runs at init (__init). Postcondition: walks the device-tree nodes matching omap_scrm_dt_match_table. For each match it maps the first register range with of_iomap; if the mapping fails it calls of_node_put on the node and returns -ENOMEM (-12), leaving later nodes unmapped. Otherwise, when the match data's index is TI_CLKM_CTRL it also sets omap2_ctrl_base to the mapping and omap2_ctrl_offset to data->offset, and in every successful case it stores the mapping in data->mem (the match data pointer is cast from const). It returns 0 after all matching nodes were handled, including when none matched.
note: checked control.c:700-721. Contract removed: the function writes globals.

name: omap4_dsi_mux_pads
prose: Precondition: dsi_id and lanes as passed by the caller; omap4_dsi_mux_syscon is a valid regmap for the register read to succeed. Postcondition: returns -ENODEV without touching any register if dsi_id is neither 0 nor 1. Otherwise it reads the DSIPHY syscon register through the regmap and returns the read's negative error if that fails; it then clears the lane-enable and PIPD fields for that DSI, ORs in lanes shifted into each field and masked to it, writes the register back with regmap_write (ignoring its return value) and returns 0.
note: checked display.c:73-102. Contract removed because the function uses the global regmap and writes a register.

name: omap_dsi_enable_pads
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: if cpu_is_omap44xx() is false it returns 0 without doing anything; if it is true it returns omap4_dsi_mux_pads(dsi_id, lane_mask): -ENODEV when dsi_id is neither 0 nor 1, the regmap read's negative error if the read fails, and 0 after the pad fields were updated (a failure of the final regmap_write is ignored).
note: checked display.c:111-116. Contract removed: the return depends on the CPU type and a global regmap.
